title: Dasakam 67 — Śrīkṛṣṇatirodhānaṃ
description: Krishna’s rasa dance with the gopikas gives way to pride, separation and searching, then to his compassionate return and their joy.

source.commentary: intake/D067/photo-captions.txt; raw intake metadata preserved in content/sources/d067/source.json

translation_note: No vetted English stanza translation is present in the supplied source bundle; translation_en is intentionally empty pending editorial review.

stanzas.sanskrit:
स्फुरत् परानन्दरसात्मकेन
त्वया समासादितभोगलीलाः ।
असीममानन्दभरं प्रपन्ना
महान्तमापुर्मदमम्बुजाक्ष्यः ॥ ६७-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sphurat parānandarasātmakena
tvayā samāsāditabhogalīlāḥ |
asīmamānandabharaṃ prapannā
mahāntamāpurmadamambujākṣyaḥ || 67-1 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna spent time with the Gopikas on the moon-lit banks of Yamuna and they were drowned in the ecstasy and supreme bliss. They were immersed in the bliss so much that they fell into pride and self-importance.

stanzas.sanskrit:
निलीयतेऽसौ मयि मय्यमायं
रमापतिर्विश्वमनोभिरामः ।
इति स्म सर्वाः कलिताभिमाना
निरीक्ष्य गोविन्द तिरोहितोऽभूः ॥ ६७-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
nilīyate’sau mayi mayyamāyaṃ
ramāpatirviśvamanobhirāmaḥ |
iti sma sarvāḥ kalitābhimānā
nirīkṣya govinda tirohito’bhūḥ || 67-2 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Each one of the Gopikas thought that Krishna, the Lord of three worlds, Lord of Lakshmi who charms the whole world is engrossed in her. Krishna in order to curb their pride and later bless them, disappeared all of a sudden.

stanzas.sanskrit:
राधाभिधां तावदजातगर्वा-
-मतिप्रियां गोपवधूं मुरारे ।
भवानुपादाय गतो विदूरं
तया सह स्वैरविहारकारी ॥ ६७-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
rādhābhidhāṃ tāvadajātagarvā-
-matipriyāṃ gopavadhūṃ murāre |
bhavānupādāya gato vidūraṃ
tayā saha svairavihārakārī || 67-3 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna identified Radha who had no pride or self-importance in her heart and took her along with HIM to a far off place and spent time with her.

stanzas.sanskrit:
तिरोहितेऽथ त्वयि जाततापाः
समं समेताः कमलायताक्ष्यः ।
वने वने त्वां परिमार्गयन्त्यो
विषादमापुर्भगवन्नपारम् ॥ ६७-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tirohite’tha tvayi jātatāpāḥ
samaṃ sametāḥ kamalāyatākṣyaḥ |
vane vane tvāṃ parimārgayantyo
viṣādamāpurbhagavannapāram || 67-4 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: After Krishna disappeared, Gopikas fell in to sorrow of separation. Together all of them, started to search for Krishna in the forest and were grief-stricken as they could not find HIM.

stanzas.sanskrit:
हा चूत हा चम्पक कर्णिकार
हा मल्लिके मालति बालवल्ल्यः ।
किं वीक्षितो नो हृदयैकचोर
इत्यादि तास्त्वत्प्रवणा विलेपुः ॥ ६७-५ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
hā cūta hā campaka karṇikāra
hā mallike mālati bālavallyaḥ |
kiṃ vīkṣito no hṛdayaikacora
ityādi tāstvatpravaṇā vilepuḥ || 67-5 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: The devoted Gopikas cried out to every tree, " O mango, O champaka, O Karnikaar, O Mallika, O maalati, O tender creepers as did you see the one who has stolen our hearts ?'

stanzas.sanskrit:
निरीक्षितोऽयं सखि पङ्कजाक्षः
पुरो ममेत्याकुलमालपन्ती ।
त्वां भावनाचक्षुषि वीक्ष्य काचि-
-त्तापं सखीनां द्विगुणीचकार ॥ ६७-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
nirīkṣito’yaṃ sakhi paṅkajākṣaḥ
puro mametyākulamālapantī |
tvāṃ bhāvanācakṣuṣi vīkṣya kāci-
-ttāpaṃ sakhīnāṃ dviguṇīcakāra || 67-6 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: One of the Gopika cried out that she saw Krishna in her imaginative vision and this doubled the grief for the rest of the Gopikas.

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वदात्मिकास्ता यमुनातटान्ते
तवानुचक्रुः किल चेष्टितानि ।
विचित्य भूयोऽपि तथैव माना-
-त्त्वया विमुक्तां ददृशुश्च राधाम् ॥ ६७-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvadātmikāstā yamunātaṭānte
tavānucakruḥ kila ceṣṭitāni |
vicitya bhūyo’pi tathaiva mānā-
-ttvayā vimuktāṃ dadṛśuśca rādhām || 67-7 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopikas identified themselves with Krishna so much that they started to imitate Krishna in their talks and actions. While Gopikas kept searching for Krishna, they found Radha rani, who went with Krishna initially but eventually got separated from HIM due to her pride.

stanzas.sanskrit:
ततः समं ता विपिने समन्ता-
-त्तमोवतारावधि मार्गयन्त्यः ।
पुनर्विमिश्रा यमुनातटान्ते
भृशं विलेपुश्च जगुर्गुणांस्ते ॥ ६७-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tataḥ samaṃ tā vipine samantā-
-ttamovatārāvadhi mārgayantyaḥ |
punarvimiśrā yamunātaṭānte
bhṛśaṃ vilepuśca jagurguṇāṃste || 67-8 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Then together all of them went searching for Krishna, till late evening. Then all of them, came back to the banks of Yamuna and kept singing praises and talking about Krishna's glories.

stanzas.sanskrit:
तथाव्यथासङ्कुलमानसानां
व्रजाङ्गनानां करुणैकसिन्धो ।
जगत्त्रयीमोहनमोहनात्मा
त्वां प्रादुरासीरयि मन्दहासी ॥ ६७-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tathāvyathāsaṅkulamānasānāṃ
vrajāṅganānāṃ karuṇaikasindho |
jagattrayīmohanamohanātmā
tvāṃ prādurāsīrayi mandahāsī || 67-9 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna, the ocean of mercy, appeared before the grief-struck  Gopikas with  an attractive smile. Krishna disappeared and reappeared again in order to make the Gopikas experience the joy & happiness double the time,

stanzas.sanskrit:
सन्दिग्धसन्दर्शनमात्मकान्तं
त्वां वीक्ष्य तन्व्यः सहसा तदानीम् ।
किं किं न चक्रुः प्रमदातिभारा-
-त्स त्वं गदात् पालय मारुतेश ॥ ६७-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sandigdhasandarśanamātmakāntaṃ
tvāṃ vīkṣya tanvyaḥ sahasā tadānīm |
kiṃ kiṃ na cakruḥ pramadātibhārā-
-tsa tvaṃ gadāt pālaya māruteśa || 67-10 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
Gopikas could not really believe their eyes when Krishna re-appeared before them and cried in joy and relief from the pain of separation. 
Bhattathiri prayed to Bhagwan, who removed the miseries of Gopikas, to protect him from his disease and afflictions.
